capabilityMatrix.note: The canary builds the upstream qpdf executable rather than reimplementing PDF operations in JavaScript.
Chromium smoke validates a deterministic one-page PDF fixture and performs a real PDF rewrite.
The canary smoke rewrites a generated PDF with --linearize and validates the result.
QPDF's built-in native crypto provider is compiled without OpenSSL/GnuTLS.
Browser execution stages explicit files in Emscripten MEMFS.
The initial QPDF browser canary is single-threaded and does not require cross-origin isolation.

notes: QPDF 12.4.1 is pinned to signed tag v12.4.1, exact commit c37f83ae468abb6cc741f43b2f6fdeb66e550ffb and the GitHub-published official source archive SHA-256.
The browser smoke starts from a deterministic one-page PDF and verifies --check, linearization, AES-256 encryption, password decryption and a final structural check.
The reviewed binary includes QPDF license/notice files plus the exact zlib license file and IJG libjpeg license-bearing README obtained from the pinned Emscripten port sources during the build.
Automatic upstream promotion and npm publication remain disabled in this release stage; both are separate reviewed follow-up work.

integration.summary: Self-host qpdf-core.js/qpdf-core.wasm plus the Zoo wrapper, stage PDF files in MEMFS, then execute ordinary upstream qpdf CLI arguments in a fresh Worker.
integration.example:
<script src="/vendor/qpdf/browser-qpdf.js"></script>
<script type="module">
const qpdf = WasmZooQpdf.loadHosted({ baseUrl: "/vendor/qpdf/" });
try {
  const input = new Uint8Array(await (await fetch("/document.pdf")).arrayBuffer());
  const result = await qpdf.exec(["--check", "/input.pdf"], {
    files: [{ name: "/input.pdf", data: input }]
  });
  console.log(result.stdout);
} finally {
  qpdf.dispose();
}
</script>
notes: No SharedArrayBuffer or cross-origin isolation is required for browser-full.
The wrapper preserves QPDF's CLI argument model and adds only Worker isolation, MEMFS staging, output collection and stdout/stderr capture.
The reviewed browser release uses QPDF native crypto and Emscripten zlib/libjpeg ports; OpenSSL/GnuTLS are not linked.
Native host filesystem paths are unavailable; files must be staged into browser MEMFS.
